drivingQuestion: Was the wall of Jericho swallowed up in its place, given that Joshua 6:20 says it fell?
outcomeNote: The apparent conflict between the baraita and Joshua 6:20 is settled: a wall whose width equalled its height was swallowed rather than merely toppled.

segments.he: וְחוֹמַת יְרִיחוֹ שֶׁנִּבְלְעָה. וְחוֹמַת יְרִיחוֹ נִבְלְעָה? וְהָא נָפְלָה, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״וַיְהִי כִשְׁמֹעַ הָעָם אֶת קוֹל הַשּׁוֹפָר וַיָּרִיעוּ הָעָם תְּרוּעָה גְדוֹלָה וַתִּפֹּל הַחוֹמָה תַּחְתֶּיהָ״! — כֵּיוָן דְּפוּתְיַהּ וְרוּמַהּ כִּי הֲדָדֵי נִינְהוּ, מִשּׁוּם הָכִי אִבַּלְעָה בְּלוֹעֵי.
segments.en: The baraita also taught that we recite a blessing for «the wall of Jericho that was swallowed» up in its place. The Gemara asks: «Were the walls of Jericho swallowed up» into the ground? «Didn’t they fall, as it is stated: “And it came to pass, when the people heard the sound of the shofar, that the people shouted with a great shout, and the wall fell down flat”» (Joshua 6:20)? The Gemara explains: «Since the width and height» of the walls «were equal to one another, therefore, they were swallowed.» Had they merely fallen it would have had no effect, as their width was equal to their height.
